title: LLM graph formation vs ESCROW on public data
question: test the public data for any ill-formed graph formation. What is the accuracy of that?

protocol.llm: streaming create-or-attach by prompting: chunks of 20 records in arrival order; prompt = current node list (name + one-line description) + records as key=value lines; JSON answer per record = existing node name or new node (name, description); node list carried across chunks; no cluster count; node-name matching = exact, then case/punctuation-insensitive (counted as loose_name_match); a referenced name that does not exist creates the node (counted as implicit_new_node); records with no parsable answer = -1
llm_arms: sampled: temperature 0.7, top_p off, top_k off, repetition_penalty 1.0, seeds 0,1,2
protocol.escrow: EscrowGraph + BatchObjective(g).install(); repair() every 100 records; final repair(full=True); record label = node with most members containing it, else -1 (background); three repetitions

metrics.ari: adjusted Rand index of record labels vs truth; -1 records form one cluster
metrics.ari_covered_only: same, restricted to records with a node
metrics.purity: sum over clusters (incl. the -1 cluster) of the majority-truth count / n
metrics.duplicate_rate: fraction of node pairs whose majority truth type is the same (the same kind of thing under two nodes)
metrics.wrong_merge_rate: fraction of nodes whose minority truth share exceeds 10 percent; also restricted to nodes with >=5 members
metrics.determinism: mean pairwise ARI between the three seeded runs' labelings
metrics.singleton_nodes: nodes holding exactly one record (node-per-record formation)
metrics.largest_node_share: fraction of scored records in the largest node (catch-all indicator; ESCROW's background is reported separately as background_or_unparsed)
metrics.value_named_nodes: LLM only: nodes whose name is a value (or key+value) copied from a member record; a value promoted to a node
metrics.tokens: prompt + completion tokens of the model's own tokenizer; ESCROW = 0

escrow_receipt_fields.justifying_key: the support key with the largest accrued evidence at mint
escrow_receipt_fields.per_key_bits: accrued evidence (bits) per support key at mint
escrow_receipt_fields.mint_bits: the candidate's TOTAL accrued evidence over all keys at mint, negative keys included; can sit below mint_price because the mint test is on the positive support subset plus outside evidence (engine.process)
escrow_receipt_fields.mint_price: price(t, |support|, n, K, e, A_n) paid at mint
escrow_receipt_fields.mint_seed: (key, value-id) the candidate was opened on
escrow_receipt_fields.members: node size at the end (records may sit in more than one node; the record label is the largest node containing it)
escrow_receipt_fields.absorbed_nodes: earlier mints merged into this node by repair, with their justifying keys

lazada.truth_granularity_note: silver types on these 1000 records: 759 distinct, 614 of them singletons, largest 16; ARI against this truth rewards one node per listing and is a granularity mismatch for any method that forms shared nodes; read duplicate/wrong-merge/determinism/tokens as the primary comparison here. The AutoPKG KG has no level above Product Type (node types: Product 36927, Product Type 16733, Attribute Key 15964, Brand 12985; edge types: has_attribute, has_key, has_value, of_type), so no coarser silver truth exists to score either method against. The silver types were derived by AutoPKG's LLM from titles and descriptions that neither method sees here; both see only the specifications map.
